about.title: Palm Desert Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Palm Desert's economy runs on hospitality, retail, landscaping, and construction, all of which carry real physical risk. When someone gets hurt on the job here, California law generally routes the claim through workers' compensation, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on a corridor like Fred Waring Drive or Country Club Drive contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside the comp claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly. We simply connect injured workers in Palm Desert with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can look at the details, explain the deadlines, and figure out whether a third-party claim adds value to what workers' comp already covers. There's no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the 30-Day Report Window
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report the injury to their employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate a claim, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: Spotting a Third-Party Claim
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be pursued separately. An attorney can review the facts to see if that applies.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Retaliating against an employee for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California. If that happens, it's worth discussing with an attorney alongside the injury claim itself.

items.question: I was hurt at a Palm Desert job site, but it wasn't really my employer's fault. Can I still file for workers' comp?
items.answer: Yes. Workers' compensation generally applies regardless of fault, so you don't need to prove your employer was negligent. That's separate from whether a third party, like a subcontractor or equipment supplier, might also share responsibility.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near Cook Street or Highway 111?
items.answer: Vehicle-related work injuries can involve both workers' comp and a potential third-party claim against another driver. An independent attorney can help sort out how those two pieces fit together.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim in California?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. That's separate from the 30-day window for reporting the injury to your employer, so it helps to understand both timelines early.
